_: Sam's injury-matrix ruling set, 2026-07-28. Collected conversationally and transcribed here by one writer (Claude). This file is the AUTHORED SOURCE: the workbook and the derived matrix are generated from it, never hand-edited. Amended same day to add 'ribs' as a 13th region, superseding the earlier twelve and the 'ribs stay unroutable' line.

declaration.text: Any exercise/region cell with no matching rule and no exception = good. From here, 'good' is always authored, never assumed.

conflictResolutions._: Ruling 1. All five adductor/pubalgia conflicts resolve to caution. Sam's reasoning on record: caution's severity behaviour (untouched 1-3, reduced 4-5, removed 6+) matches how he would coach it, and the old pubalgia 'avoid' thinking survives in the stricter plyo exceptions, which stand.

newRegionPatternRules._: Ruling 2 + amendment + ribs follow-up. Every pattern x new-region cell not listed here carries NO rule. Sam added the pressing patterns to ribs on 2026-07-28: bench compression and overhead work are the mechanism.

newRegionMuscleRules._: Ruling 2 + amendment. Muscle-axis rules for the new regions. ribs has NO muscle-axis rules by ruling. The Traps -> neck rule was REMOVED on Sam's follow-up ruling: 'Traps' is never a primary muscle, so the rule was unreachable, and an authored rule nothing can reach is a defect, not a keepsake. Neck cover for Shrugs is now a named exception instead.

extraExceptions._: Sam's follow-up ruling. Named exercise exceptions authored directly rather than reverse-engineered from an existing rating. Shrugs is the most neck-loading lift in the pool but has primary 'Upper back' and pattern isolation_upper, so it matched no neck rule and fell to the declaration. The two chest-supported rows are bench-compressed PULLS, which the pressing rule cannot reach. Incline Y Raise joins them on Sam's ruling (2026-07-28) — same bench-compression mechanism, and its own cue says 'Chest on the incline'; it is isolation_upper, which no ribs pattern rule reaches. | 2026-08-26 (recorded in commit 63cc38e4, transcribed 2026-09-03): Sam on Front Squat for a bad shoulder — "remove it from good". The rack-position squats (Front/Box/High Box) match Back Squat's own shoulder caution. | 2026-08-27 (63958d24, transcribed 2026-09-03): the Bible's hamstring section rules quad-dominant lower work "usually okay" and names box squat / controlled squat / step-up as the swaps, so Leg Press, Box Squat, High Box Squat, Goblet Squat, Step Ups and Leg Extension carry hamstring good — LOOSER than the squat pattern rule, by Sam's own text. | 2026-08-28, R-267 (006fa6c1 + 01334a5a, transcribed 2026-09-03): "Ratings include indirect support/loading." Every lower-body lift whose prescribed load is a held or racked free weight (the 19 free-weight load profiles in the load map) cautions shoulder, elbow and wrist/hand where the rules said good; the two Copenhagen planks caution shoulder and elbow for the same support-loading reason. Guard: simpleInjurySafetyTruth in test:canonical-weekly-compiler. No axis of this model reads the prescribed load, so these are named. | 2026-09-03, R-363: Sam ruled the app is right on the squat elbow/wrist cells the sheet had not carried (Back Squat, Front Squat, Box Squat) — already covered by the R-267 block above. Adductor Rockback: Sam ruled its thirteen ratings on 2026-09-03 from the rated drills nearest to it (Horse Stance Hold, Groin Squeeze, Crab Hold, Sleeper Stretch); the Groin muscle rules give groin and knee caution, the declaration gives quad, hamstring, calf, ribs and neck good, and the six cells the model cannot reach are named here: hip, ankle/foot and lower back (kneeling, end-range rock), shoulder, elbow and wrist/hand (weight through the arms, lighter than Crab Hold's avoid). | 2026-09-04, R-364: Adductor Rockback's six named cells moved OUT of this list — the drill now enters through the complete intake like the other 32 recovery exercises, so its thirteen ratings are authored on its tags row (docs/EXERCISE_INTAKE_RECOVERY_2026-09-04.md) and the pipeline lifts them as intake exceptions. Under R-364's preserve-every-contraindication clause its groin cell is Avoid (the pool contraindication), stricter than R-363's Caution.

conditioning._: Ruling 3 + amendment. Ruled BY HAND, no new taxonomy. STRICTER-WINS: existing avoids (sprint hamstring/calf) stand above these blanket cautions. Sam's authored principle, recorded verbatim for the future quality-grid unit: 'caution any region the modality's equipment or movement meaningfully uses; severity does the rest.' | 2026-09-04, R-364: the three zone-1 walks join as the 'walk' family — on-feet locomotion cautions the lower body like the run family, without ribs (no impact); they were never matrix rows before because they carried no tags.
conditioning.principle: caution any region the modality's equipment or movement meaningfully uses; severity does the rest.

sprint.note: lower body per Sam's enumeration (groin, hip, quad, knee, ankle/foot) plus hamstring/calf where existing avoid dominates; shoulder for arm drive; ribs per the amendment.

bike.note: existing knee stands; NO wrist/hand on bikes

untouched.note: Easy Bike stays unruled-to-good deliberately — it is the escape hatch. MetCon, Light Circuits, Easy Swim: existing cells stand, rest good.

routing._: Ruling 4 + amendment. Free text -> region. Entries with two targets are BLOCKED: the resolver is single-target in the mechanism, so they are recorded as ruled but NOT implemented, per Sam's own stop condition. Amended 2026-08-02 (Sam, LR-27 divergence table, PARKED_QUESTIONS_2026-08-01 §5): shin/shins -> calf ADDED (single-target), and quadricep (singular) corrected to quad — the knee route was a sheet typo.

dual._: EMPTY BY RULING. Sam ruled routing SINGLE-TARGET everywhere on 2026-07-28: hip flexor -> hip, achilles -> calf, upper back -> shoulder. Duals are off the table; episode-identity semantics (bucket equality in coachInjuryTargetResolver) stay untouched. Logged as a possible future refinement ONLY if athlete complaints expose coverage gaps.

exceptions._: Ruling 5. All 18 stand as authored. Any that now agree with the new rules dissolve into them automatically.
